text:
Marta: heads-up — multiple customers seeing 5xx/gateway timeouts on hosted API starting ~09:03 UTC. Support case CS-2148 (Acme) has consistent 502s on /v1/generate. Error spikes line up with a sharp drop in cache hit rate.

Devon_sre: seeing the same in grafana — cache error budget exploded. p50 stable, p95 jumped from 250ms -> 1.6s, 5xx rate from 0.2% -> ~9%.

Samir_infra: I dug into the KV/prefix cache telemetry. Redis connection failures and timeouts on the prefixed shard pool. Example logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:03:15Z] ERROR KVCacheRedis: connect failed, errno=111 (connection refused)
[2026-03-15T09:03:15Z] WARN KVCache: prefix_pool=shard-12, cmds_in_flight=142, avg_cmd_latency_ms=520
[2026-03-15T09:03:16Z] ERROR RouteProxy: upstream timeout after 1200ms, route=/v1/generate, downstream=client-xyz
```

API sample error returned to customers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"backend_error","message":"prefix-cache timeout: upstream redis timed out"}
```

Jia_engineer: customers repro steps (from Acme):
1) call POST /v1/generate with a 1k token prompt (no streaming)
2) observe 502 after ~1.2s consistently
curl example: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-13b","input":"hello world"}'
```

Devon_sre: initial mitigation options — (A) disable prefix/KV caching for prod (fast rollback), (B) increase cache client timeout + enable retries with jitter, (C) route traffic to a backup region/pool without prefix caching.

Samir_infra: I can flip a feature flag for prefix cache at the control plane. Command to disable (test on staging first):
```bash
# admin API (control plane)
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.ai/admin/feature-flags 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"flag":"prefix_cache.enabled","value":false,"scope":"prod"}'
```

Marta: do we have a risk of increased per-token cost or latency if we disable cache? yes — hit rate is usually ~72% so expect higher GPU work, but better than 5xx. Communicate to affected customers (CS/SE).

Devon_sre: I'm going to open a pager for infra and propose a quick toggle: disable prefix cache for the affected shard pool (shard-10..shard-14). Samir, can you prepare the flag and a rollback?

Samir_infra: preparing now. I'll post the exact flag and the verification steps when ready.

Infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0315-01 (priority P1) — assigned to devon_sre, samir_infra.

Theo_customer: FYI — we saw a complete outage at 09:04 and then intermittent 502s until ~09:12. Thanks for the quick response.

Jia_engineer: testing notes for verification after toggle:
- check /metrics prefix_cache_hit_ratio >= previous baseline? Will drop but should not cause 5xx
- ensure 5xx rate for /v1/generate drops to <0.5%
- run a small canary with 5% traffic for 15m before full rollover

Devon_sre: action plan timeline:
- 09:10 toggle prefix cache off for shard-10..14 (canary 5% traffic)
- 09:25 evaluate metrics (latency, 5xx, system load)
- 09:35 if stable increase to 100% for those shards
- 09:50 follow-up postmortem start

Marta: I'll update CS ticket CS-2148 and send a status note to Acme. Also prepare an email to customers who hit 5xx with recommended mitigation (retry with exponential backoff).

Samir_infra: toggle executed (09:11). Control plane response: {"status":"ok","changed":"prefix_cache.enabled","scope":"shard-10..14"}.

Devon_sre: metrics after toggle: 5xx rate dropped to 0.6% within 2 minutes. p95 latency increased ~120ms — acceptable. Rolling out remaining shards after 10m stability window.

Marta: thanks everyone. Postmortem owners: samir_infra (infra lead), jia_engineer (runtime), devon_sre (oncall). Please collect logs, redis slowlog, eviction stats, and the upstream redis cluster events.

Samir_infra: preliminary root cause hypothesis: planned maintenance on redis-cluster-3 applied a config that triggered a rolling restart and caused connection thrashing on prefixed pools. Will confirm with the infra provider.

Devon_sre: follow-ups: add circuit-breaker to cache client, lower critical dependency surface (graceful fallback when cache errors), and validate alerting thresholds for prefix cache error rate.

Marta: marking thread resolved for now. Will link incident INC-2026-0315-01 to CS-2148 and send customer-facing summary after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
